Thanks again for your time today — good discussion. Recap below so we’re aligned and so our engineers/procurement have a single source of truth. I’ve attached the initial Q&A and a draft mutual action plan (MAP).

Key pain points you highlighted
- User-perceived latency on real-time suggestions (product UI) spikes under load and degrades conversion.
- Cost unpredictability for high-volume inference during peak periods.
- Data residency & auditability for EU customers (GDPR + corporate policy).

Goals you shared
- 99th percentile request latency <= 250ms for short completions (<= 256 tokens) during normal traffic; 95th <= 180ms desirable for first-response.
- Sustained throughput target: 500 requests/sec (avg request ~40 tokens) with headroom for 2x burst.
- End-to-end monitoring, request-level traceability, and exportable audit logs for compliance.

Technical notes / asks for Redwood follow-up
- Confirm recommended deployment topology (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for the above SLOs in EU region.
- Provide a cost estimate at 500 rps and for a 2x burst scenario.
- Share model variant recommendations (quantization, KV cache behavior) for your chat/suggestion workload.
- SOC2 / security questionnaire items for procurement (we’ll include the SOC2 pack + deployment checklist).

Immediate next steps (what we’ll deliver by EOD Wed)
1) Send a concise technical topology sketch and a recommended configuration for a pilot (Marissa will add ops notes).
2) Draft MAP with milestones for a 6-week pilot: data handoff, POC tests, SLO acceptance criteria, procurement timeline.
3) Provide initial cost ballpark and a list of required artifacts for your security/compliance team.

Attachments: stargazer-poc-answers.pdf; mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Marissa/Ben on the tech sketch.

Thanks Jasmine — helpful recap. A couple clarifying points from our side:

- The 500 rps target is our expected peak for the recommendation engine (we currently average ~120 rps globally). We expect bursts to 1k rps during campaign windows.
- Latency budget: 99th <= 250ms is a hard requirement for the inline suggestions path; the background batch reranks can tolerate higher latency (~1s).

Can you confirm whether the recommended pilot will be on Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) in eu-west-1 or if you suggest Hosted with regional routing? Our security team prefers Dedicated but wants to weigh cost.

Also looping Procurement (procurement@stargazer.ai) — can you include a list of contract items we should expect (data processing addendum, EU data residency clause, termination/exit terms)?

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Ethan — quick ops-oriented writeup to supplement Jasmine’s notes. I sketched a topology (attached) and a configuration we’d propose for the pilot. High level:

Topology recommendation (pilot):
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated in eu-west with cross-region failover to eu-north for resilience. Dedicated gives predictable tail-latency and isolation for compliance.
- GPUs: a small pool of A10G-equivalent nodes with a pool sized to sustain 500 rps (40 token avg). Estimate: 6–8 GPUs baseline with autoscale to 16 for bursts (fast scale-up path).
- Model variants: primary model = open-llm-chat-3b (fp16) for quality; quantized int8 variant (reduced memory) for burst routing. We’ll run throughput tests to validate 99p latency with int8 fallback.
- KV / prefix caching: enable request-scoped KV cache for repeated conversation prefixes and persistent per-user KV for suggestion seeds — reduces tokens served and improves latency.
- Batching: continuous batching with a 10–20ms batching window for suggestion requests; explicit low-latency route (no batching) for critical first-response flows.

SLO mapping & acceptance criteria (pilot):
- Latency: 99th <= 250ms for critical route (<=256 tokens) measured at the CDN edge -> app server -> Redwood edge.
- Throughput: sustain 500 rps for 30 minutes with p99 constraint; burst to 1k rps with transient degradation allowed but falling back to quantized variant with <500ms p99.
- Quality tolerance: top-line quality regression <= 3% (as measured by your prompt set evals) when routing to quantized variant during bursts.

Operational notes:
- We’ll provide tracing hooks and a short Prometheus metrics export (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, batch sizes).
- Cost ballpark: approx €1,800–€2,400/day baseline (6–8 GPUs) including Managed Runtime + Networking; burst provisioning increases variable costs — we’ll provide a 3-scenario cost sheet in the MAP.

Attachments: topology-sketch.svg (ops sketch). I’ll coordinate a short load-test run with your infra team to validate the numbers.

—
